subject: Proposal: modular add-ons vs per-seat metering for AtlasPilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlaspilot.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: AtlasPilot pricing options and two commercial paths

Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, attached is a concise comparison that lays out two commercial paths we commonly recommend for teams like AtlasPilot: (A) modular add-ons on a flat tier (predictable commit + optional feature packs) and (B) per-seat metering (usage-driven, easier to start, more variable spend). I attached a simple tier comparison (AtlasPilot_Tier_Comparison.xlsx) and a starter SOW we can use for a short pilot.

High level:
- Modular (Tiered + add-ons): predictable monthly commit, lower incremental unit economics for heavy token workloads, supports reserved GPU pools for latency-sensitive routes. Good if you need predictable spend and want to lock in a performance profile.
- Per-seat metering: pay for active seats / monthly MAUs with optional token overage. Low upfront commitment, great for pilots and fast-growing teams, but per-token costs are typically higher at scale.

Questions we flagged for pricing:
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens (rough ballpark) and peak concurrency needs for the inference routes you care about.
- Whether you require dedicated capacity (redwood dedicated) for latency SLOs / data isolation.

Proposed next steps:
1) You review the attached worksheet and mark your preference.
2) If modular, we propose a 6-month committable pilot at 50% of the list increment for the first 3 months (trial discount) with standard step-down thereafter.
3) If metered, we can do a 90-day pilot with a 20% platform credit applied to the first invoice.

I also included an outline of the add-ons you asked about (long-context, KV caching, priority routing). Let me know if Procurement wants a single consolidated invoice or PO flow; we can support both.

Available earliest for a quick pricing call: tomorrow 11/26 between 09:00–12:00 PST.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172

Attachments: AtlasPilot_Tier_Comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-draft.pdf (proposal)
From: Samir Patel <samir@atlaspilot.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlaspilot.com
Date: 2026-11-25T10:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPilot pricing options and two commercial paths

Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A couple questions before we loop in procurement formally:

1) Can you show a simple 5k/month equivalent for both approaches (modular commit vs per-seat) so we can see the delta? We want the option to scale down after the pilot without penalty.
2) If we pick modular, what is the on-ramp if our usage stays below the committed level? Any credits/rollover?
3) For per-seat, how do you handle seat churn in month 2 / month 3 — do we get prorated refunds or just credits?

We're leaning toward starting with the per-seat model for a 90-day pilot, but I'd like to see the 5k/month examples so I can present to our CEO.

Also — we need guaranteed 99.9% availability on the inference endpoint for our demo windows; will that require Dedicated?

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel | Head of AI
AtlasPilot
samir@atlaspilot.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPilot pricing options and two commercial paths

Ben / Rishi —

Quick internal note with the recommended commercial approach for this ask. I'm drafting language we can give Samir that balances predictability with pilot flexibility. Key points:

- Offer a 90-day pilot on per-seat metering with a 25% credit applied to their first two invoices (gives them runway). This answers their desire to start low friction.
- Include an optional toggle to convert to the modular tiered plan on day 91 with a look-back at trailing 30-day token usage to set committed level. If they convert within 60 days of pilot end, cap price increases for 6 months.
- For scale-down protection on the modular side: allow a 30% roll-forward credit for unused committed tokens applied over the next 2 billing cycles (not full refunds). This keeps predictability but doesn't overexpose Redwood.
- Seat churn on metered: we do credits (not refunds) for seats removed mid-billing cycle, applied to next invoice; standard practice is prorated credits to avoid awkward negative invoices.
- Availability: 99.9% at our hosted API tier is best-effort; Dedicated (reserved capacity) is required for an SLA-backed 99.9% with uptime SLA and faster latency guarantees. Quote Dedicated as an add-on in the SOW.

Pricing levers to give them in writing:
1) Pilot credit (25% applied to first two invoices)
2) Conversion protection (cap increases for 6 months)
3) Commitment smoothing (30% roll-forward for modular unused tokens)

Ben — please draft a brief follow-up to Samir that puts the above in plain bullets, includes a simple 5k/month comparison row for both approaches, and links to a short DocuSign for the pilot SOW. Rishi — want your eyes on the 30% roll-forward terms and whether we can tighten that to 20% for finance (we can offer 30% as initial ask).

Thanks — keep it short and option-oriented.

Hannah

Subject: Re: AtlasPilot pricing options and two commercial paths — pilot proposal

Samir —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per Hannah's note, here's a concise option table at a 5k/month reference point plus the pilot ask. See bullets below and attached SOW (SOW-draft.pdf). If that looks ok we'll send a DocuSign for the 90-day pilot.

5k/month illustrative (normalized)
- Modular (Tiered + add-ons):
  - Monthly commit: $5,000 (includes base tier and basic add-ons)
  - Long-context pack: +$1,200/mo (optional)
  - Dedicated routing (if required for 99.9% SLA): +$2,500/mo
  - If actual token usage < committed, 30% of unused tokens roll forward as credit applied across next 2 invoices.
- Per-seat metering:
  - Equivalent spend target: $5,000/mo based on projected 12 seats active @ $400/mo + token overage if > baseline.
  - Pilot credit: 25% applied to first two invoices (reduces first two bills to $3,750).
  - Seat churn: prorated credit applied to next invoice for removed seats.

Pilot offer summary:
- 90-day per-seat pilot with 25% credit on first two invoices.
- Option to convert to modular tier on day 91 with a look-back at trailing 30-day usage to set committed level; if converted within 60 days we cap increases for 6 months.
- Dedicated capacity quoted separately if you need an SLA-backed 99.9% window for demos.

Next steps:
1) If Procurement confirms, we will send DocuSign link for the pilot SOW. (link: https://docusign.example/packet/AP-2026-042)
2) Provide a PO or email confirmation of pilot intent; we can start provisioning once DocuSign is complete.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk through the SOW with your procurement team.

Best,
